AC EVIDENCE (verified against merged main b86a1b4c293, Gerrit 2064 MERGED). AC1: 'grep -rn "def _shadow" src/rebar' returns exactly ONE definition, _operation_config.py:271, with the underscore retained so the oracle measures the right name; all three MCP surfaces carry 'from rebar._operation_config import _shadow' (_mcp_llm.py:19, _mcp_writes.py:33, _mcp_reads.py:42). AC2: exactly one argparse converter 'def _positive_int(value: str) -> int' at _cli/_parsers/_common.py:19, imported by all THREE twins (request.py:15, bridge.py:15, reconcile.py:17); the only other definition is the out-of-scope namesake. AC3: _lib_ops.py:27 imports the shared helper and its 10 call sites forward repo_root, enforced by an AST test that walks every _shadow( call in the module and fails on any that omits the keyword. AC4: _config_resolvers.py does not appear in the landed diff at all (numstat match count 0), so the (raw, default) namesake that returns a default rather than raising is untouched. AC5: the landed tests/ delta is 205 added / 0 deleted in a single NEW file - no existing assertion was edited - and all 11 tests pass.

GUARD TEETH PROVEN BY MUTATION, not merely asserted: appending a second 'def _shadow' to src/rebar/_store/hlc.py made test_each_helper_is_defined_exactly_once FAIL with "_shadow: ['rebar/_operation_config.py:271', 'rebar/_store/hlc.py:160']", then restored. The guard scans _SRC.rglob('*.py') by AST rather than by text, so a re-introduced copy cannot merge silently - which is the durability property the parent epic exists to establish, and the property that 4329 and 111a were found to be MISSING.
